H1.name: risk-state switch: equal-weight sectors <-> defensive trio
H1.rule: Decision at each session close t: if T(t)=1 hold the equal-weight defensive leg, else the equal-weight risk-on leg; execute at the next session close when the state changes. Within a leg, rebalance to equal weights at the last session of each calendar month (decision) executed at the next session close; between rebalances weights drift. Always fully invested in equities; never cash. Warm-up: first decision when ^GSPC has 200 closes and (D/H) every sector in the leg has >= 253 sessions; XLRE/XLC join the risk-on leg at the first month-end after their 253rd session.

riskon_leg.D_H: equal weight of all eligible sector SPDRs
riskon_leg.L: equal weight of the 12 French industries

reasons_from_D_only: Risk-on leg = equal-weight sectors: no D sector-selection rule beat equal weight (J2* = B5). SPY adds a cap-weight bet the defensive leg lacks; a declared high-beta set would need D outcomes to choose.
Defensive leg = XLP/XLU/XLV: peak-to-trough the trio beat SPY in all five D episodes with SPDR data (2000-02 +31.5, 2008-09 +19.2, 2011 +12.9, 2015-16 +9.6, 2018Q4 +10.7 pp).
Switch on risk state, not sector momentum: at the 2000 and 2007 peaks the D sector RS rules did not hold the defensive trio as a group.
T rather than J1-E: J1-E exited before the trough in 2 of 6 D episodes and never left equities in 2011, 2015-16 and 2018Q4, the three episodes where the trio beat SPY by 9.6-12.9 pp.

Faster trigger with a defensive fallback: on D, T's false risk-off spells against cash cost 3.73%/calm-yr (B3). With a defensive fallback a false spell costs the risk-on-minus-defensive spread rather than equity premium minus bills, because the defensive leg's beta to the market is below the risk-on leg's. That asymmetry is the argument for the faster T over J1-E.

T rather than T-and-credit: on D J1-B and B3 exited on the same dates in all six episodes; credit's lower false-pivot count matters less when false pivots are cheap, and credit is not available on L (repo DBAA from 1986), which would make H1 H-only.

primary_contrast.name: beta-matched rotation value (replaces the draft's X1 as primary, review finding 1)
primary_contrast.definition: Daily difference D_t = r_H1,t - r_ref,t, where r_ref,t = r_H1,t on days H1 holds the risk-on leg (difference 0), and on days H1 holds the defensive leg r_ref,t = beta_t x r_on,t + (1 - beta_t) x r_cash,t, with beta_t = OLS beta of the defensive leg's daily returns on the risk-on leg's daily returns over the 252 sessions ending t-1 (>= 200 observations), clipped to [0, 1.5]. The statistic is the annualised mean of D_t. It measures whether rotating into defensives beat holding the same market exposure in the risk-on leg plus cash during T's risk-off spells, and so removes T's market-timing term, which v1 already measured on L (B3).
primary_contrast.costs: H1 net of its own costs; reference costless
primary_contrast.secondary: X1 = static mix of the two legs at H1's risk-on share, built on the same month-end rebalancing calendar as H1 (review finding 4); reported, not tested

H1.L_clean: For the primary statistic: largely clean. It removes T's market timing, so it is not a re-test of B3; no industry-level return on L has been computed. Not clean for the trigger: T's state path and its market-level timing on 1928-1997 were seen in v1. General knowledge of the history applies (see samples.L).

H2.name: crisis de-risk: exit to cash only when recession confirmation and the trend trigger agree
H2.rule: Identical to v1 J1-E: SPY weight 0 if (T and M) else 1; daily rule, trades only on change; remainder in cash.
H2.why_unchanged: J1-E was the best J1 candidate on D (P1 +2.96%, raw p 0.06; G2, G3 and all G6 risk tests except exit-before-trough met). Changing its earlier trigger after seeing D (for example to credit) would be a new rule chosen on D - a forking path. It is carried unchanged so that D-selection is the only contamination.
H2.primary_contrast: annualised mean daily return of H2 minus X2 = w x SPY + (1 - w) x cash, w = mean H2 SPY weight on the window tested
H2.L_clean: NO. J1-E's market-level performance on 1960-1997 was computed in the v1 Stage D long tier, and M (real-time Sahm) does not exist before 1959-12, with no substitute that is both real-time and long. H2 is H-only.

power_from_D_variance_only.statement: H2 cannot detect any plausible effect on H. Moreover, H's largest SPY drawdown (Feb-Mar 2020) ended before real-time Sahm could confirm, so H2's max-drawdown condition is very unlikely to be met; its realistic outcome is L0.

third_hypothesis.considered: J3-C (risk-state cross-asset rotation) vs its primary comparator R1 (exposure-matched equal-weight 7 sleeves)
third_hypothesis.why_left_out: On D its primary contrast R1 was +3.33% with raw p 0.13 (Holm 0.63); the only strong number was the secondary R2 vs GTAA, and promoting the secondary would be selection on D. It has no L sample (cross-asset ETFs start 2002-2007; the J3 proxy tier would rest on J1-B's credit flag, which is not available before 1997), so it would be H-only with a minimum detectable effect of about 11 pp/yr. Adding it would raise Holm m to 3 and cost power for H1 without a realistic chance of a result. The reviewer agreed.

decision_rule.why_pooled_plus_sign: H alone cannot see less than about 3.8 pp/yr, so separate H significance would be a formality. L carries about 91% of the pooled weight, so the pooled test is mostly an L test; requiring H > 0 and both L eras > 0 is what stops one period from carrying the result. At a true 1.5 pp/yr the joint rule passes about 80% of the time; at 1.0 pp/yr it is closer to a coin flip.

L1_accepted_historical.H1: all of: primary statistic significant at the fixed-sequence alpha (or Holm, per parent choice) on the pooled sample; pooled estimate >= +1.0 pp/yr; H estimate > 0; both L eras > 0; significance and effect conditions still hold at 2x costs; pooled stress capture vs SPY <= 0.80, where pooled stress capture = product over all named L and H episodes of (1 + H1 return peak->trough) minus 1, divided by the same product for SPY (L: French market TR); H1 CAGR >= risk-on-leg-alone CAGR - 1.0 pp/yr on L and on H separately.
L1_accepted_historical.H2: all of: Holm p < 0.05 on H; H estimate >= +1.0 pp/yr; holds at 2x costs; max drawdown <= 0.70 x SPY max drawdown on H; CAGR >= SPY - 2.0 pp/yr on H.
